title: Paid Leonardo call whose response fails validation loses the generation id / cost receipt
fix: On parse failure after a successful 2xx paid POST, return a distinct 'charged but unparsed' error variant (carrying generation_id when it can be recovered, or a flag), and split Transport into never-sent vs possibly-sent so callers can reconcile or ledger the spend; for remove-bg keep the cost and drop only invalid assets.
scenario: POST v1/generations succeeds and is billed, but the body has a cost shape wire::cost_record rejects (amount with >6 decimals or exponent form from apiCreditCost, e.g. 1e-7), or remove-bg returns one result whose url/contentType fails validation (wire.rs:203-217). The whole call returns ArtError::Response, so the caller never sees generation_id or the CostRecord for money already spent; a 45s transport timeout after send (transport.rs:77) is likewise indistinguishable from never-sent. Tests pin the Response error (leonardo.rs:233-253) so the loss is deliberate-looking but unledgered.
note: Changes the ArtError public surface and the policy for unledgered paid calls; owner/Director decision on error taxonomy.

title: PassedMessage / MessageFacts derive Debug and expose raw chat text
fix: Replace the derived Debug on MessageFacts and PassedMessage with a manual impl that prints ids and flags and omits `text` (a redacted placeholder), plus a test asserting the format does not contain the text.
scenario: MessageFacts (Debug, Clone) carries the full chat `text`; PassedMessage derives Debug (pool.rs:618). Any future `tracing::debug!(?passed)` or a {:?} in an error path writes viewer chat text to logs, contradicting README 'No message text is retained' and the no-chat-in-logs law. Only the keyword pool needs the text, and only transiently.
note: Local, one failing test (format!("{:?}") contains the text) proves it.

title: seal_roll never checks that GuardedDraw policy matches the Roll's actual pool and weight rules
fix: Derive the pool-dependent policy flags from RollRules at GuardedDraw/seal time (or assert in seal_roll that policy.subscriber_only==(pool==Subscribers), channel_points==(pool==Redeemers), free_entry_equal_odds==free_join_equal_odds) and return Error::Invalid on mismatch.
scenario: The same fact is held twice: DrawPolicy.subscriber_only / channel_points / free_entry_equal_odds / paid_weight vs RollRules.pool (Subscribers, Redeemers) / free_join_equal_odds / weight_curve. seal_roll only reads draw.check().result == Blocked. A prize Roll with Pool::Redeemers and a concave activity curve sealed with a default GuardedDraw (channel_points=false, free_entry_equal_odds=true) yields CheckResult::Ok with no warning, so the guardrail the README promises is bypassed by configuration drift; the adapter must keep two structures in sync by hand.
note: Choosing which side is authoritative changes the DrawPolicy/RollRules API and the cc-core convert::policy mapping.

title: Cohort caps are a post-hoc check, so a cap can deterministically fail and consume the draw
fix: Either resolve caps before sealing (exclude or pre-select by cohort so the sealed entry set cannot violate them) or reject at seal_roll when the frozen entry set cannot satisfy the caps; at minimum refuse seal when limit(winner_count)==0 and all entrants belong to that cohort.
scenario: cc-verify samples winners without knowing cohort caps; Roll::validate_winners rejects the result afterwards. With winner_count=1 and cap 1/2, CohortCap::limit floors to 0 (pool.rs:651), so any winner in the capped cohort aborts the cast with 'cohort cap exceeded'; the sealed attempt is consumed (draw_tests.rs:183 pins this). With a small or all-capped cohort pool the draw can never succeed, and the owner may re-seal repeatedly until the beacon yields an acceptable result (a grinding path).
note: Touches the byte-exact v1 sampling algorithm or lifecycle semantics (consumed attempt is pinned behaviour); owner decision.

title: Failed cast leaves a DrawSealed row with no terminal audit row
fix: Append a terminal ledger event (e.g. DrawFailed with draw_run_id and a coarse reason code) before returning the error from cast_*, after checking the seal audit exists.
scenario: finish() returns early on 'cast predates seal', winner/cap validation failure, or a bad quicknet round / seed (draw.rs:211,234,249); a SealedDraw dropped without casting does the same. The ledger then holds DrawSealed forever with no Draw or failure event, so an audit reader cannot tell abandoned, failed and in-flight attempts apart, even though the attempt is consumed.
note: New LedgerEvent identifier must land in cc-types/cc-store first per contract rule.

title: seal_roll trusts caller-supplied seal time and margin against the real clock
fix: In seal_roll compare `at` with recorded_at (reject skew beyond a few seconds) and require a documented minimum margin_s; add tests for a backdated seal.
scenario: seal_roll accepts any `at` and any margin_s>0; recorded_at is stored but never compared with `at`. A caller passing a stale `at` (or margin 1) selects a drand round that is already published at seal time, defeating the unpredictability guarantee while a valid seal is audited. The only guard is cc-core's lifecycle.rs which passes now() and checks the target round after publication.
note: Choosing the skew tolerance and minimum margin is a policy decision.

title: QuicknetClient::fetch has a hardcoded host and no seam, so its parsing and guards are untested
fix: Add a base-URL constructor (cfg(test) or a pub(crate) with_base) and a local mock or split the reply decoding into a pure function fed with the fixture JSON, then test oversize, chained signature, wrong round and the real public-2.json shape.
scenario: The URL is fixed to https://api.drand.sh. The 16 KiB cap, previous_signature rejection, round mismatch check and UpstreamRound deserialization (beacon.rs:242-293) have no test; the real-reply fixtures are parsed through serde_json::Value in tests/quicknet.rs, never through UpstreamRound. A regression in this path surfaces only on draw day and consumes the draw.

title: UpstreamRound uses deny_unknown_fields on a third-party reply
fix: Drop deny_unknown_fields on UpstreamRound (keep it on the local Writ/BeaconRound formats) and keep the previous_signature and signature checks.
scenario: If drand adds any field to /public/{round} (it has extended responses before), serde_json::from_slice fails with Error::Json on draw day, and with a consumed-on-failure draw the stream loses the cast although the signature would verify. Strictness is not needed here: trust comes from verify_round, not from the shape.
note: Loosens a strict boundary the repo law treats as pinned; owner call on tolerance vs strictness.

title: CLI usage errors are reported as 'Unverified:'
fix: Use a distinct prefix/exit code (e.g. exit 64 with 'Usage:' for argument errors, 'Unreadable input:' for IO) and keep 'Unverified:' for verification failures only; extend cli.rs.
scenario: `cc-verify` with no or bad args prints 'Unverified: Usage: cc-verify ...' and exits 2, the same as a failed proof; file-too-large or unreadable file also say 'Unverified'. A script or user cannot distinguish a tampered writ from a mistyped command.
note: Local, testable by asserting exit code and prefix for no-argument invocation.

title: Code gates (file-cap, hygiene, boundaries, secrets) walk untracked and git-excluded trees, so pnpm lint is red in a normal local checkout
fix: Build the inventory from git: `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` (filtered by existing extension/prefix rules) for file-cap, hygiene and boundaries, keeping the empty-inventory refusal; or at minimum add .claude, .contest, .hackathon, .spark, .ai, film to the ignored set. Add a closure case that seeds a 401-line file under .claude/worktrees/x and expects the gate to ignore it. Decide separately whether secrets should still scan untracked-but-present dirs (keep, but skip binary extensions incl .webp .mp3 .mp4 .wav).
scenario: walk() is a raw readdir that skips only .git/node_modules/.pnpm-store/target/dist/coverage; productCode() only excludes root-anchored prototype/, docs/, .personas/. It never consults git, so untracked dirs listed in .git/info/exclude are inventoried: .claude/worktrees/* (2410 of the 3371 walked files, each a full repo copy incl. its own prototype/ and docs/ which the root-anchored excludes miss), .contest (190M), .hackathon, film. Verified by running node scripts/check.mjs: file-cap reports e.g. .claude\worktrees\spark-e2e-night\prototype\app-lottery.js 479 lines and .contest\...\react-dom_client.js 16036 lines; hygiene reports prototype keydown/swallowed-catch hits; boundaries reports 'workspace deep import @castle-control/ui/duel' from the worktree copies, and the worktree package.json files (same package names) are folded into the owner/packages maps and graph (false cross-package and cycle edges). check.mjs exits 1, so tooling-lint, every package lint (package-gate lint calls check.mjs) and pnpm gate fail locally whenever a spark/contest worktree exists, while CI (clean clone) passes. secrets also reads 7486 files (~235MB incl. webp/mp3/mp4 because only png/jpg/woff2/ico are skipped).
note: 2fb10f3 + test; also fixed own lane.rs cap break 7664c89

title: e2e harness tests (including native-host CSP parity) and e2e typecheck/eslint are run by nothing: not pnpm gate, not CI
fix: In tooling-test also walk e2e for *.test.ts and pass them to node --test --test-isolation=none (Node >=24 strips types; imports already use .ts extensions); add `eslint e2e` and `tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.offline.json` (or the real tsconfig) to tooling-lint. Update ci-shape/closure proofs for the new inventory.
scenario: tooling-test walks only scripts/ for *.test.mjs; e2e has no package.json so pnpm -r skips it; playwright testMatch is **/*.spec.ts. e2e/harness.test.ts (route inventory vs real navigation.ts, loopback policy, and 'overlay harness CSP equals the native host CSP' parsing crates/cc-obs/src/overlay.rs) and e2e/styles.test.ts only run when someone follows the README by hand. If cc-obs changes its CSP template or navigation.ts gains a route form, the gate stays green and only the advisory (continue-on-error) lanes job eventually shows a symptom. Likewise eslint (tooling-lint covers scripts/ and eslint.config.js only) and tsc never touch e2e/*.ts.
note: e2e harness tests red today (9 routes vs 8, CSP lacks /push/gatehouse)

title: Per-package lint re-runs the whole-repo check.mjs in every workspace and eslint skips contract scripts and e2e
fix: Run check.mjs once (tooling-lint only) and drop it from package-gate lint; add packages/contract/scripts and e2e to the eslint invocation in tooling-lint (expect to fix whatever surfaces).
scenario: Each of the 6 workspace packages has lint=package-gate.mjs lint, which runs check.mjs with cwd at the repo root (full boundaries/hygiene/file-cap/secrets over every file, TS-parsing each), and tooling-lint runs it again: 7 identical whole-repo passes per pnpm lint (one pass measured ~10s on 3371 files => ~70s redundant; scales with any untracked tree). Separately `eslint src` (line 21) and `eslint scripts eslint.config.js` (tooling-lint) leave packages/contract/scripts/*.mjs (codegen.mjs, parity.mjs, test-codegen.mjs, i.e. the contract gate itself) and e2e/*.ts un-linted by any step.
note: 0cff1cb: check passes 7 -> 1 (eslint half demoted: eslint broken here)

title: Hygiene 'no as unknown as' and 'no swallowed catch' are trivially bypassed
fix: Unwrap ts.isParenthesizedExpression before the AsExpression test and also reject `as never`; add a check for call `.catch(<arrow with empty block or void/undefined body>)`. Add closure cases for each.
scenario: The double-assertion check requires node.expression to be an AsExpression directly, so `(value as unknown) as T` (ParenthesizedExpression in between) and `<T><unknown>value` pass; `as never as T` passes. The swallowed-catch check only flags a catch clause with zero statements, so `promise.catch(() => {})` / `.catch(() => undefined)` (identical swallowing, no CatchClause node) passes. No current hits in tracked code (git grep), so this is a latent hole in a repo-law gate.
note: Local AST change, each form provable by a seeded closure case.

title: Boundary gate cannot see type-position imports, so a deep relative or private import hides in `typeof import('...')`
fix: Add a ts.isImportTypeNode branch (argument is a LiteralTypeNode of string) that calls inspect(); then replace e2e's type imports with the declared public door or an explicit documented exemption.
scenario: visit() handles only Import/ExportDeclaration and CallExpression with ImportKeyword/require. ImportTypeNode (`typeof import('../packages/contract/src/index.ts')`) is never inspected. e2e/core-launch.ts:8-10 does exactly this with a cross-package relative path that the gate would reject as 'cross-package relative import' if written as an import declaration; any future `type X = import('@castle-control/ui/private').Y` also bypasses the deep-import and undeclared-dependency rules.
note: tightening breaks e2e/core-launch.ts (cross-package typeof import); fix that file first

title: closure-proofs.mjs is a near byte-copy of prove-gates.mjs
fix: Delete closure-proofs.mjs (or make it import prove-gates) and point docs/PLAN.md at `pnpm gate:proofs`.
scenario: Two 92-line scripts implement the same proof runner; only the evidence path (env override) differs. package.json and CI use prove-gates.mjs; docs/PLAN.md:58 still tells people to run closure-proofs.mjs. A fix to one (scratch handling, the status check) will silently miss the other, and the stale one hard-writes docs/gate-evidence.md.

title: e2e README says the lane is not in CI, but ci.yml runs gate:proofs and pnpm e2e (advisory)
fix: Reword to 'advisory CI job (continue-on-error), not in pnpm gate'; drop the 'Expected red on base' comment.
scenario: README states 'This lane is not part of `pnpm gate` or CI yet' while .github/workflows/ci.yml job `lanes` runs `pnpm e2e` with continue-on-error and ci-shape.test.mjs pins it. A reader trusts the README and assumes red e2e in CI is unexpected/unrelated, or that no artifact upload exists. A stale comment in e2e/journey-beacons.spec.ts:325 ('Expected red on base') likewise describes a removed state.
note: unprovable (README)

title: 36-state Atlas test runs in one test under the default 30s timeout
fix: test.setTimeout(120_000) or split per style (test.describe loop) so failures name the state; measure first.
scenario: playwright.config sets timeout 30_000 and only journey-lots overrides it. 'atlas switchers ... across all 36 states' loops 6 styles x 2 layouts x 3 shots with ~15 awaited expects, an all-images waitForFunction and a bounding-box evaluate per iteration in one test; on a slow CI Chrome it can hit the limit and fail as a timeout rather than an assertion, with no indication of which state was reached.
note: unmeasurable (needs Playwright)

title: Contract door throws an opaque 'Invalid contract value' with no method, path or HTTP status
fix: Carry safe diagnostics only: method name, ajv instancePath and keyword per error (never data values, to keep chat text out), and the HTTP status on the non-envelope error path; tests keep asserting toThrow.
scenario: checked() discards validator.errors and names neither method nor field, and invokeMethod (line 17 of the error branch, `if (!response.ok) throw parseError(text)`) throws JsonParseError/'Invalid contract value' when a non-2xx body is not a valid envelope (stale token behind a proxy, HTML error page). A core/contract schema drift in production surfaces as an identical generic error for every method and cannot be told from an auth failure; the HTTP status is lost.
note: unprovable under node (vitest-only)

title: Beacons lazy-subpath method list is hard-coded while Gatehouse derives it from the registry
fix: Derive beaconsNames from `name.startsWith('beacons.')` (excluding none today) like gatehouse, and add a registry-coverage assertion mirroring test-gatehouse-registry for beacons (and steward).
scenario: gatehouseNames is computed from schema.methods by prefix with test-gatehouse-registry.mjs guarding it, but beaconsNames (line 170) and stewardNames (169) are literal lists. A ninth beacons.* method added to cc-types gets p/r validators in the eager module but is silently omitted from beacons-validators/beacons-validation and the ./beacons and root-barrel handles; test-codegen only asserts the hard-coded count 8, so nothing fails. Two rules for 'which methods belong to the beacons door'.
note: Small generator change; red-once by adding a synthetic beacons.* method to a schema copy and expecting it in the subpath.

title: JSON-door usage scan only recognises the literal text `JSON.parse`
fix: Also flag any zero-argument `.json()` call and element-access/alias forms of JSON.parse in authored code; use `project` for the door path comparison; add cases to test-codegen.
scenario: Law says every boundary value is parsed in one place (door.mjs), but usages() flags only a call named `parse` whose receiver text is exactly `JSON`. `response.json()`, `request.json()`, `JSON['parse']`, `const { parse } = JSON` and `const p = JSON.parse` all bypass the door without a parity defect. No current `.json()` callers (git grep over apps/packages/e2e), so latent. The exemption also compares against join(root, ...) rather than the `project` argument.
note: Local AST rule, provable with seeded fixture files in the existing usages() scratch test.

title: Cold `cargo run` for schema/registry export has a 120s hard timeout
fix: Build once with `cargo build -p cc-core --bin export-registry -p cc-types --bin export-contract` (no timeout, or 15 min) then run the binary under the short timeout; and name the timeout in the thrown error.
scenario: exportRegistry (and exportSchema at codegen.mjs:26-27) spawnSync cargo run with timeout 120000. gate.mjs runs contract check/parity right after `cargo fetch` and before any build, so on a cache-miss CI runner (windows-latest, cache keyed on Cargo.lock) cc-core's first compile of its dependency tree may exceed 120s; spawnSync then returns error ETIMEDOUT and the gate fails with 'spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT' with no hint that it was a slow build, not drift.
note: unmeasurable (cold CI build)

title: A definitive seal refusal (blocked_by_policy, invalid, rate_limited) locks the Lot room until the app is restarted
fix: Keep the lock only when the outcome is uncertain (transport failure, unavailable, upstream, internal, conflict). Clear it on definitive pre-commit refusals (invalid, blocked_by_policy, unauthorized, not_found, rate_limited) and on local parse failure, and assert locked in the policy-block test.
scenario: seal() publishes locked:true before the RPC. The core answers blocked_by_policy (or rate_limited with retry_after_ms), or call() fails local param parsing at line 84-85 before anything is sent. perform() only publishes a notice, so locked stays true. editable() is then false, and Refresh, Select, Edit and Seal are all disabled in rooms/lottery/core.tsx. The notice says 'Review the policy reasons before trying again. Retry after 1000 ms' (copy request_errors), but no retry is possible and the room shows 'uncertain seal must be reconciled'. The test at lots-core.test.ts:300 asserts the notice but never asserts locked.
note: Which error codes prove a seal did not happen is a seal-safety policy decision the owner pinned ('a lost response must never reopen a potentially sealed roll').

title: --steward-live without native services advertises the Steward as live though no engine exists
fix: Only emit steward:'live' when native services are present (steward_live && services.is_some()), or reject --steward-live without --client-id in Options::parse. Update the host test that pins the metadata round-trip.
scenario: Options::parse accepts a lone --steward-live. CoreHost::start builds AppState::new(Registry::with_status()) with no services, so steward.ask returns 'no Steward engine is configured' (host_tests.rs:250). launch() still passes self.steward_live, so the UI gets steward:'live'. inspector.tsx:54 then labels the Steward 'Steward · live' and StewardConnection.live is true, while every ask fails.
note: host_tests.rs deliberately pins the flag as metadata for offline launches, so changing it reverses a pinned behaviour.

title: A single unparseable event makes the event socket reconnect forever and pins the UI on 'connecting'
fix: After N consecutive parse failures on the same seq, skip the event (advance since_seq and invalidate) or surface a distinct 'event schema mismatch' state. Add a back-off to the fixed 1000 ms retry.
scenario: onmessage parses with parseEvent. On failure it calls interrupt() and closes the socket, and since_seq only advances after a successful parse. connect() reconnects with the same since_seq, so the server replays the same event. Each cycle publishes 'Core connection interrupted; status is unknown' and nothing ever recovers. A core event kind newer than the bundled schema triggers this.
note: Skipping versus surfacing an unparseable event is a policy choice and changes the read model's states.

title: Core Drill keeps a hand-typed recording name over a newly imported recording
fix: Clear recordingName when state.recording?.recording changes, for example by keying the field state on the imported recording id or resetting it in the import click handler.
scenario: recording = recordingName ?? state.recording?.recording. Once the user types in the Recording name field, recordingName is never reset. A later importRecordingJson publishes state.recording for B, but the field still shows the old text. Run replay, Save baseline and Compare use the stale name and hit the wrong or a missing recording.
note: Local component state, provable with a render test: type a name, import, assert the field shows the imported id.

title: Editing a core draw moves it to the end of the draw list
fix: Replace in place: snapshot.draws.map(item => item.draw_id === saved.draw_id ? saved : item), appending only when the draw is new.
scenario: edit() builds draws as [...snapshot.draws.filter(other id), saved]. Committing a new winner count or saving appearance moves the edited draw to the last option of the draw select. load() restores the core order, so the order flips between actions. gatehouse upsertRule maps in place, so the two stores disagree.
note: One-line local change with a unit test on draw order.

title: Rule bench evaluates the whole accumulated chat on every render of the core Gatehouse room
fix: Memoise messages and the evaluateDraft result on [state.chat, state.rules, draft], and cap or window the accumulated chat pages.
scenario: ConnectedGatehouse recomputes messages (a map over state.chat.items) and evaluateDraft (regex compile plus four text variants per message) on every render. A render happens on every snapshot publish (busy flips, notices, each read) and every bench keystroke. moreChat appends pages with no cap (gatehouse-core.ts:180), so after many 'more' clicks the work grows without bound.
note: memoised draft eval 20 -> 10; RuleBench child still evaluates

title: Pattern preview calls an unmatched ] or } 'invalid' although the Rust gate treats them as literals
fix: Escape a literal unmatched ] and } when building the JS source, or return unsupported_by_gate. Add vectors to crates/cc-gatehouse/src/pattern_vectors.json so both sides are pinned.
scenario: A rule pattern like 'end]' or 'a}' compiles in the Rust regex crate (literal). compilePreviewPattern returns refuse('invalid') at line 53 for ] outside a class. For } the JS 'iu' RegExp throws and line 81 returns 'invalid'. The bench shows 'invalid' and blocks saving a rule the gate would accept. The refusal should be 'unsupported_by_gate' at most, and pattern_vectors.json has no such vector.
note: TS preview now reads unmatched ] } as literal like Rust; [] a] still refused (open)

title: Fixture cast ticket shows two buttons that run the same action
fix: Drop one button, or give them distinct actions if two were intended.
scenario: Before the cast, FixtureCast renders 'Cast the lots · rehearsal' and 'Start simulated draw'. Both call port.start(). Two visible controls with the same effect confuse keyboard and screen-reader users, and a test can only distinguish them by label.
note: Which label to keep is UX copy; tests (lots.test.tsx, journey.test.tsx) may pin both.

title: Proof bundle download is a data: URL anchor under a navigation allowlist that refuses non-same-origin URLs
fix: Verify in the built shell. If blocked, allow the exact data:application/json download in on_navigation, or serve the bundle through a core RPC download or a clipboard copy.
scenario: The 'Download proof bundle' link uses href=data:application/json with a download attribute. main.rs on_navigation returns same_origin(url, origin), which is false for a data: URL. If WebView2 routes the click through the navigation handler, the download is silently blocked and the user cannot save the proof bundle. Not run in the real shell.
note: unmeasurable without built Tauri host; any fix widens navigation allowlist = owner decision

title: Core rule rows are keyed by the whole serialized rule, so saving a rule name remounts the row and drops focus
fix: Use row_key={rule => rule.rule_id}.
scenario: WindowedRows row_key={rule => JSON.stringify(rule)}. After upsertRule returns the new name, the key changes, React unmounts the CoreRule form and mounts a new one, and keyboard focus returns to the page. The uncontrolled name input also loses unsaved text if the list refreshes mid-edit. The key is rebuilt for every rule on every render.
note: One-line change, provable with a test that the same input node survives a save.

title: Clearing a numeric draw-setup field (cooldown, prize value) snaps back and cannot be retyped
fix: Move cooldown and prize value onto useTextDraft, committing only valid integers like the winners field.
scenario: Cooldown onChange passes valueAsNumber to rule(). An emptied field gives NaN. validDraw rejects it with a notice and the controlled input still shows the old value (value={rules.cooldown_s}). The user cannot clear the field to type a new number, and the same happens for prize value at line 113. The name, keyword and winners fields use useTextDraft to avoid this.
note: Local fixture-room component, provable with a render test that clears and retypes the field.

title: Round-source label treats a hard-coded 2023 timestamp as 'recorded' with no shared constant
fix: Derive the label from a core-provided source flag, or add a cross-language drift test that reads the Rust constants like moderation-bench.test.ts reads pattern_vectors.json.
scenario: lotsRoundLabel decides a seal is simulated if simulated===true or sealed_at === '2023-08-23T15:09:28Z'. That is a copy of the sentinel in crates/cc-core/src/lots/recorded.rs, and the quicknet chain hash at line 31 is a second copy of live_beacon.rs. If the recorded plan changes, a recorded seal is labelled 'Live-trusted quicknet' with no failing test on the TS side.
note: drift guard test

title: Beacon burst timing input cannot be cleared to retype
fix: Hold a string draft in the component like TimingField (apply valid values live, resync on blur).
scenario: Operator selects the burst field and presses Backspace to empty it: valueAsNumber is NaN, session.change rejects it (Number.isInteger(NaN) false), no listener fires and the controlled input snaps back to the old value, so only select-all-and-type edits work. rooms/moderator/output.tsx TimingField already solves this with a draft buffer (parity).
note: Local to one component, provable with a render test that fires an empty change.

title: Curve control-point inputs reject clearing and show float noise
fix: Round the displayed percent (e.g. Math.round(x*1e6)/1e6) and keep a local string draft for both number inputs.
scenario: Intensity input is value={point.intensity*100}: after a drag or arrow edit (e.g. 0.29) it renders 28.999999999999996, and clearing either number field yields NaN which editor.move ignores so the field snaps back and cannot be retyped.
note: Local component change with render test.

title: Unsaved curve draft discarded whenever the visual object identity changes
fix: Key the memo on a content digest (JSON of visual.curve) or preserve the draft when the confirmed curve is unchanged; or disable Refresh while phase is editing.
scenario: EditableKindlingCurve memoises the editor on [visual, port]. Pressing Refresh Beacons (core.tsx:53-55) reloads visuals as new objects; the editor is recreated and an in-progress, unsaved control-point draft is silently lost with no notice, even when content is identical.
note: draft kept across refresh

title: Rule bench save/propose result is not announced to assistive tech
fix: Use role=status (aria-live polite) for non-error notices.
scenario: On success the notice (saved, proposed, pending) renders in a p with role undefined, so only errors (role=alert) are announced; a screen-reader user gets no feedback after Save as watching.
note: second role=status breaks rule-bench.test.tsx

title: Rule form catch collapses every failure to rule_invalid
fix: Surface the validator message when it is an Error from our own validators (or map to refusal copy) instead of a fixed string.
scenario: proposeWatchingRule/proposeCommand/on_save can throw specific errors (compile refusal copy, only watching pattern rules may be edited, a rejected upsert); the bare catch discards them and the user always sees the generic invalid-rule text, with nothing logged.
note: Local; test by throwing from on_save.

title: OBS status failure is swallowed with no code or notice
fix: Route the rejection through refusal(error) into notice (keep obs unknown).
scenario: In refresh(), a port.status() rejection (unauthorized, rate_limited, core down) is handled by a callback that only publishes obs unknown; the cause is dropped and, if visuals load, the notice says Choose the scene..., so the operator cannot tell a dead or unauthorized core from OBS being off, while the sibling visuals() branch maps the error through refusal().
note: Local; test with a rejecting status transport.

title: Steward tell() leaves busy stuck and drops typed text if routing throws
fix: Wrap in try/finally for setBusy(false); restore the input text when the turn is the failure reply.
scenario: tell() calls setBusy(true), clears the input, awaits ask, then routeStewardTurn(...) and only then setBusy(false) with no finally; if a navigation callback throws, the bar stays Drafting and refuses further input. The typed text is also cleared before the call so a failed turn loses it.
note: Local with a throwing on_open test.

title: Core Beacons port created by render-phase mutation with swallowed error
fix: Create the port in a useMemo/state initialiser and show a safe code from the thrown error.
scenario: CoreVisualsRoom does connection.port ??= createCoreBeaconsPort(...) during render and catches any throw with a bare catch returning a generic message; the validation failure reason is never logged or shown, and the side effect is repeated under StrictMode or concurrent re-renders.
note: premise-false: bare catch unreachable

title: ClockTime builds an Intl.DateTimeFormat per row render and throws on bad timestamps
fix: Hoist the formatter to module scope and fall back to the raw string when the Date is NaN.
scenario: Every ledger/chat row render constructs a new Intl.DateTimeFormat (costly) and clock.format(new Date(at)) throws RangeError for an invalid at, which would unmount the whole room if any row carried a bad string.
note: guard only; formatter hoist blocked by a test that spies Intl at render

title: Replay panel recomputes counts and a lowercased text scan on every render
fix: useMemo counts and filtered on [messages, filter, query, marked].
scenario: With 4200 fixture lines, each render (1 Hz playback tick, every keystroke in search) runs filter for three verdict counts, the draft count twice, and lowercases every message_text; none is memoised.
note: scans 40 -> 0 (fixture path only; CoreChat rebuilds array)

title: Replay baseline 420 duplicated between playback and model
fix: Export one initial replay count constant from the model and import it.
scenario: ChatPlayback hardcodes 420 (latest, arrivals) while moderation-model.ts:32 independently sets replay_count: 420; changing one silently breaks the arrivals count.
note: unprovable (refactor)

title: Resized sample boards leave a quarter of new tiles unclaimed via modulo 4 over 3 sides
fix: Decide intent: use % sides.length, or comment and test the deliberate unclaimed pattern.
scenario: sizedBoard picks STUDIO_SAMPLE_BOARD.sides[(column+row)%4] but there are only 3 sides, so index 3 is undefined and those tiles become unclaimed in S/L boards; counts and banner chips for S/L disagree with M in a pattern that looks accidental.
note: Needs owner decision whether the gaps are intended sample design.

title: Art failure copy does not warn that credits may already be spent
fix: For upstream/internal codes append a line that the charge is unconfirmed and should be checked at the provider.
scenario: On a thrown error (upstream or internal where the provider may have charged) the UI shows only Art request failed: code. No automatic retry was made., while the confirm step said it costs credits; the operator is not told to check the provider balance or receipt.
note: Copy and cost-disclosure wording is an owner/policy choice.

title: Vote bar never reconnects after an HTTP refusal (503) so OBS shows a blank bar until refresh
fix: On error with readyState===EventSource.CLOSED close and schedule a backoff reconnect like connectOverlay (extract a shared helper); keep native retry for CONNECTING.
scenario: OBS loads /gatehouse/current before the vote-bar source is set (host.vote_bar unset) or while the client permit pool is full; /push/gatehouse answers 503 (crates/cc-core/src/overlay/vote_bar.rs:88-94). EventSource goes to CLOSED and never retries on a non-200, onerror clears the root, and the comment claims native reconnect. The bar stays empty for the whole session. overlay.ts handles exactly this case with a 2s..30s backoff retry.
note: Local; provable with a Stream double like overlay-chain.test.ts; needs bundle rebuild and fingerprint update

title: Viewer panel tile labels computed from a different tile set than the war-table preview
fix: Take the label origin from the map (pass min_column/min_r or the full tile list into createViewerControls) so both views share one labelling.
scenario: Label origin (min_column, min_r) is recomputed from controls.tiles here and from scene.tiles in war-table.ts:165. If the host passes only a subset of the map as selectable tiles (e.g. map A1..D4, controls omit the first row/column), the panel button says Tile A1 while the map title says Tile B2 for the same hex, so the viewer picks the wrong-looking tile.
note: Changes the createViewerControls/renderViewerPanel API shape and which set is authoritative for labels; host usage not in this context

title: Scripted packages stop working after any stream error because module scripts do not re-execute
fix: Append a cache-busting fragment/query per build generation, or reload the document when a scripts package is rebuilt after clear.
scenario: A package with privileges.kind==scripts is applied; a stream error calls clear() (replaceChildren) and the reconnect re-applies the same hash, creating new script elements with the same URL. ES modules evaluate once per document, so the entry never runs again and the scene stays without its script behaviour; old modules also have no teardown on package change.
note: LANE C: ?build=N cache-bust works (1->3 evals) but old modules lack teardown, DOM-owning scripts run twice per reconnect; fix commit 5d2dcbe not merged, bundle not rebuilt

title: Rejected push snapshots are invisible to the operator
fix: On rejection set root.dataset.snapshotRejected (count or reason code, never payload text) alongside the existing diagnostics dataset.
scenario: Host and renderer disagree on the contract (stale bundle after a contract change): every snapshot fails parseBeaconsRenderSnapshot and receiveSnapshot returns false without any signal. The OBS source shows a frozen or empty scene and nothing in the DOM or console says why.
note: Local, testable with receiveSnapshot double; bundle rebuild required

title: Re-selecting the same writ file does not re-run verification
fix: Reset fileInput.value = "" after reading the file (inside the change handler) so the same file can be chosen again; rebuild index.html.
scenario: User imports writ.json, gets REJECTED, fixes the file on disk and picks the same path again: the input value is unchanged so no change event fires and the stale REJECTED stays.
note: Local; testable with the existing html-check file double (value reset); regenerate artifact

title: Imported writs silently depend on bundledSamples[2] as the trust anchor
fix: Embed the official chain as its own named constant in generate.ts and assert in html-check that the imported-official case verifies against it.
scenario: The anchor is a magic index into a list ordered by generate.ts (two simulated then public cases). Reordering or removing samples makes chain undefined (imported drand writs then show UNVERIFIED with no explanation) or points at the simulated test key, with no test tying index 2 to the official chain.
note: Local generate.ts/page.ts change, regenerate artifact

title: Static check bans every question mark in site HTML instead of the replacement character
fix: Use /[—�]/ for the intended em dash / replacement check.
scenario: The class [—?] contains a literal ? where U+FFFD was meant. Any copy with a question mark or a URL query string fails the check, while a real encoding-replacement character U+FFFD in the HTML passes undetected.
note: One-character regex fix, provable by a sample string

title: Audit row carries no outcome or failure reason; refused, rules-only and timeout calls look like successes with model_served None
fix: Add a sanitized outcome label (Outcome::label plus Failure variant name) to LedgerEvent::Engine in cc-store, with the cc-types/cc-store identifier landing first, then pass it from Audit::append.
scenario: A live classifier call times out or returns unparseable text -> fallback() yields RulesOnly/Refused, but the single LedgerEvent::Engine row holds only class/provider/model_selected/model_served/cost. An operator reading engine.jsonl cannot tell Timeout from Parse from NotAdmitted from CloudOptIn, nor count fallback rate per class; the live stall/timeouts the engine is designed around are invisible after the fact.
note: Changes the LedgerEvent::Engine wire/contract shape in cc-store (new identifier lands in cc-types first, own delivery).

title: Probe reports installed:false for keychain, supervision and timeout errors
fix: Match the Err: propagate Failure::Auth/Supervision (keychain and custody failures) and map only Unavailable (missing exe) and Timeout to installed:false/signed_in:false.
scenario: probe() is called with key_label whose vault.load fails (Auth), or on a host where Tree::new returns Supervision, or capture times out after 10 s. capture() returns Err, `let Ok((true, bytes)) = version else` swallows it and returns Probe{installed:false, signed_in:false}. A present, working CLI is reported as not installed and the real cause is lost. The same swallow applies to the auth capture (Err(_) => false).
note: Local to health.rs; a failing test with a rejecting Keychain proves it (no caller outside the crate yet).

title: Local-endpoint response requires a usage object; servers that omit it make every call a Parse failure
fix: Mark `usage` #[serde(default)] (Usage already defaults every field); keep the cloud path strict only if cost must be exact.
scenario: An OpenAI-compatible loopback server returns a valid chat completion without `usage` (or with `content: null` on a refusal). Response.usage has no #[serde(default)], so serde_json fails -> Failure::Parse. measure_floor then records 0 correct for all six cases and the live lane silently falls back to rules-only, with no signal that the server was fine but the schema was too strict. Local calls are priced at zero anyway, so usage is not needed.
note: pinned by simulated_fixture_usage_shape

title: Stop failure replaces the real turn error, and a failed exit status is masked by parse errors
fix: Ignore (or log by label) the stop error and return the original result; check status.success() before finish() and return Unavailable.
scenario: turn() times out (Failure::Timeout), then stop() cannot reap the child within 2 s and returns Supervision; `stop(..).await?` returns Supervision and drops the Timeout, so the audit/fallback reason is wrong. Similarly a CLI that crashes with empty stdout reaches parser.finish() which returns Parse before the non-success status check at line 234 can mark Unavailable.
note: ordering fix only; stop() error not provable

title: Startup sweep fails permanently on any non-empty or non-directory ULID-named entry
fix: Decide a policy: remove entries recursively only after verifying they are real directories under root (symlink check already exists), or skip-and-continue with a counted warning instead of aborting construction.
scenario: A previous run left <root>/<ulid>/ containing a file (a child wrote into its cwd, which is the run dir) or a stray file named like a ULID. sweep() uses non-recursive remove_dir (line 98) or returns Supervision at line 95, so SpawnDoor::new fails on every start and the whole CLI lane (steward) is dead until someone hand-deletes the directory. Run::drop also silently leaves such dirs (let _cleanup).
note: Destructive deletion policy (recursive delete of child-created paths is explicitly avoided by the code comment).

title: AnswerShape is silently ignored for non-live classes, contradicting complete_with_shape docs
fix: Document that shape applies to live classes only (or make the Steward pass an explicit no-validation shape variant) so the contract is not a silent no-op.
scenario: A caller passes AnswerShape::Custom to complete_with_shape with class Batch/Offline (CLI or an Endpoint route installed via RoutingTable::set). The `live(call.class) &&` guard skips shape.accepts, so invalid text is returned as Outcome::Model. The doc says the caller's parser is applied with the 'normal ... fallback ladder', and cc-core steward depends on the skip (it calls complete with default Verdict on Batch and parses a Writ itself). Also api.rs:117 would force json_object for a Verdict-default Endpoint route on Batch.
note: Pinned behaviour relied on by steward; choice between doc fix and a new AnswerShape variant is an owner decision.

title: Outcome and Reply derive Debug and print chat-derived model text
fix: Hand-write Debug for Outcome that prints only the label and Failure, eliding text (assert_eq in tests keeps PartialEq).
scenario: Outcome::Model{text} holds the model's reply to a prompt built from viewer chat (classifier) or owner prompt (steward). Derived Debug on Outcome/Reply (and any {:?}/assert failure/panic payload in a caller) prints that text to logs or test output, against the rule that chat text never lands in Debug/errors. No current caller formats it, but the derive makes it one careless unwrap away.
note: Local impl; a test asserting format!("{:?}") omits the text proves it.

title: RoutingTable::set ignores route.model for CLI-transport rows
fix: Reject set() of a Cli route whose model differs from the provider model, or document that the model field is ignored for Cli routes.
scenario: set(Route{class:Batch, transport:Cli, model:X, ..}) stores X, but get() overwrites row.model with the claude/codex model from the table for every Cli row, so X is silently discarded and the audit's model_selected shows a different model than the one the caller configured.
note: Local to model.rs; a set/get round-trip test fails today.

title: A ledger fault blocks forget_user and retention expiry, which never touch the ledgers
fix: For ForgetUser and ExpiredRecordings check only purge_pending (not ledger_fault) in execute_purge, since they delete SQLite rows only; keep ledger_fault gating for ledger and data reads.
scenario: An append_ledger write or sync fails (disk full) -> ledger_fault stays true (ledger.rs:288) -> forget_user and purge_expired call ready() and return LedgerIntegrity. A viewer erasure request is refused, and expired raw recordings are kept past the cap. Any spawn_retention_task would also exit permanently on its first error. Only purge_all works, and README says only that one is kept available.
note: Changes the pinned fail-closed contract in README and tests (failed writes or corruption block normal operations); owner must decide whether erasure and expiry count as normal operations.

title: map_user overwrites a login's owner, orphaning the previous user's data from forget_user
fix: Key mappings by (user_id, login) so reassignment adds a row instead of replacing one, and have forget_user resolve every user_id that ever held the login; or add forget by user id.
scenario: map_user(1,"foo"), insert a recording for user 1, then a different account takes the renamed-away login: map_user(2,"foo") flips foo -> 2 (ON CONFLICT(login) DO UPDATE). User 1 now has no viewer_mappings row. forget_user("foo") erases user 2, and user 1's recordings can no longer be reached by any login (forget keys on login), so they linger until retention.
note: Changes the viewer_mappings schema (migration) and forget semantics; a privacy-policy decision on who a login refers to.

title: read_ledger re-reads and re-verifies the whole ledger file on every call, and callers call it per capture
fix: Verify the full chain once at open, then keep the lines (or a per-user decision index) in memory, extended by append_ledger. Alternatively add a bounded tail or filtered reader for the callers that need one decision.
scenario: The ledger is append-only and unbounded until purge_all. Each read_ledger does a full file read, JSON parse, canonical re-serialization and SHA-256 of every line. cc-gatehouse live_capture.rs:64, lane.rs:373 and held.rs:52 call it on the live path, so cost grows with ledger length and stalls the store while chat is flowing. Not measured.
note: 511dbc1 ledger cache by len+mtime; 1003 -> 3 verifications. Residual: same-length mtime-restoring edit served from cache

title: Retention is keyed on caller-supplied item.at with no bound at insert
fix: Reject, or clamp to now, an at later than the insert time plus a small skew in insert and insert_configuration; or stamp a store-side recorded_at column for expiry.
scenario: insert stores at=item.at unchecked. An item with a far-future at (clock skew or a bad upstream timestamp) is never matched by 'at < cutoff', so raw viewer content outlives the retention cap. Not traced to any current caller that supplies a future at.
note: Needs a decision on clamp versus reject, and on whether replayed or simulated events may carry future times.

title: Overlay server task failure is never observed
fix: Expose a health or join method (or a watch for task exit) so cc-core can surface an overlay-down status.
scenario: axum::serve returns an io error (accept failure) and the JoinHandle result is discarded. Overlay keeps handing out url() while nothing listens, and OBS shows a blank browser source with no diagnostic. Drop only aborts the task.
note: premise-false: axum serve retries accept errors

title: Every non-100 OBS status collapses to Error::Rejected, losing the code
fix: Map a few known codes to distinct Error variants (for example ResourceExists, NotFound), keeping the fixed-diagnostic style and no peer text.
scenario: CreateInput failing with 601 (resource already exists, the normal case when a source is recreated) or 600 (scene missing) is indistinguishable from any other failure. The caller cannot offer a fix or an idempotent retry. tests/assumptions.rs:96 pins the collapse to Rejected.
note: Changes the public Error enum, which the existing tests pin.

title: Blocking keychain read runs inside the async connect, beyond the timeout's reach
fix: Run the read through spawn_blocking (PasswordReader is already Send + Sync), or read the password before starting the timed section.
scenario: reader.read calls keyring synchronously on the async task. A locked or prompting credential store blocks the runtime worker, and the 5s BUDGET timeout cannot preempt it because it is not an await point.
note: needs connect_with_reader signature change

title: Live ask drops a valid core writ when any unrelated queue publish happens mid-request, orphaning it
fix: Replace whole-snapshot identity with a check on the affected proposal only (previous proposal object identity for amend, absence of writ_id for new) so select/focus do not invalidate.
scenario: Streamer asks the Steward (model call takes seconds); meanwhile focusing any ProposalCard (inspector.tsx on_focus -> queue.select) or a chamber focus publishes a new snapshot object. getSnapshot() !== before is true, so the successfully proposed writ is discarded with 'could not confirm this draft'; the core keeps a proposed writ no UI can reach (id unknown to #writs).
note: Local to LiveSteward, provable by a failing test that calls queue.select/focus while ask is pending.

title: Live seal reports permanent unknown outcome when an unrelated queue publish lands during the seal call
fix: Compare only the sealed proposal (find by id === the proposal captured before) rather than the whole snapshot; keep uncertain for genuine mismatches.
scenario: Hold completes, seal RPC in flight, user focuses another proposal card (queue.select publishes). Core replies sealed and valid, but getSnapshot() !== before returns unknownSeal; #uncertain keeps the id forever, so the UI shows 'outcome unknown, reconcile' for a seal that succeeded and the proposal is never marked sealed locally.
note: Seal outcome semantics are owner-sensitive authority behaviour; confirm a confirmed core seal should apply locally despite unrelated queue activity.

title: Unconfirmed tear leaves core writ torn while local proposal stays pending and sealable
fix: Mark the id uncertain (or reconcile via a read) when the tear call itself threw after dispatch, mirroring seal.
scenario: steward.writ.tear succeeds at the core but the reply is lost or fails validation: catch returns the generic failure ('queue is unchanged'), no uncertain mark, proposal remains pending with a live Hold. A later seal is refused by the core and then marks the id permanently uncertain.
note: Needs an owner decision on tear uncertainty semantics.

title: Amending a restyle draft with a custom request (or reverse) always conflicts on title
fix: Keep a stable title per draft (one title for both actions) or let draftDesign reuse current.title on update.
scenario: draftDesign sets title 'Restyle' vs 'Custom design'. queue.addOrUpdate (queue.ts:53) rejects any update whose title differs, so SimulatedSteward.amend('design a quiet look for the urn') or DesignSession.amend with the other action on an open draft returns 'A draft update must preserve its identity and field keys.' for a valid amendment.
note: One-line local change, provable with a failing session.amend test across actions.

title: Every Restyle/Custom click creates a new pending design proposal; drafts pile up unbounded
fix: Amend the open draft for this artifact when one exists, else draft new.
scenario: DesignControls calls session.draft (new design-N id) on each click; only the latest is displayed in DesignFocusView, earlier drafts stay pending in the shared queue and Inspector until manually torn.
note: UX direction: one open draft per artifact vs many.

title: Draft pane copy says to choose Restyle even when a draft exists but is unpreviewed; seal disabled without explanation
fix: When pending && !preview show 'Preview the draft to enable the hold.'
scenario: After clicking Restyle a pending draft exists but preview is undefined, so the pane still says 'Choose Restyle or Custom design' and the proclaim hold is disabled with no hint to press Preview draft.
note: Local copy fix with a render test.

title: ConsensusChart keeps a stale selected index and emits NaN geometry for bad timestamps or zero window
fix: Derive an effective index clamped to results.length; skip or clamp non-finite points and shares.
scenario: If results shrinks below the selected index, result falls back to results[0] but the select value matches no option and shows blank; Date.parse of a malformed at/series.at or window_s 0 yields NaN polyline points silently (Math.min/max keep NaN); share above 1 plots outside the chart.
note: Local pure-render change, provable by a render test.

title: Hold to speak never ends if the pointer is released outside the button; no keyboard path; no caller wires it
fix: setPointerCapture on down and end on lostpointercapture, add a keyboard hold, or remove the dead prop until wired.
scenario: onPointerDown starts speech; releasing after dragging off the button fires pointerup elsewhere (no pointer capture, no pointerleave), so on_speak_end only fires on blur and capture stays open. git grep finds no caller of on_speak_start.
note: Voice input is an unshipped feature; owner decides to wire or remove.

title: StatusChip and Pennant throw during render for an empty word; no error boundary exists in the app
fix: Render a visible fallback word instead of throwing, or add a root error boundary.
scenario: A stamp chip or Pennant given a blank data-driven label (e.g. hex-table.tsx side.label) throws in render; git grep finds no ErrorBoundary in apps or packages, so the whole React tree unmounts to a blank window.
note: Policy on render-time invariants vs an error boundary needs an owner call.

title: RuleTable re-implements the windowing rule with a different clamp than WindowedRows
fix: Have RuleTable call rowWindow from windowed-rows.
scenario: visibleRange clamps start to total-1 while rowWindow clamps to total-count; row-h, table-window and overscan are duplicated. A future fix to one (for example the sticky-header offset, which RuleTable ignores because thead sits inside scrollTop) will not reach the other.
note: e22f05a; 37 -> 0 disagreements

title: FieldGroup emits a hint id nothing references and a dynamically inserted status region
fix: Clone the child with aria-describedby or accept a describedby prop; keep the status node mounted and fill text (as Notice does).
scenario: The control is an arbitrary child, so aria-describedby is never set to the hint id and screen readers do not announce the hint. The role=status result node is created with its content already present, which many readers do not announce.
note: hint id wired; always-mounted role=status blocked by tests counting status nodes

title: Breadcrumb hard-codes hash routes while taking back_href as a prop
fix: Accept keep_href and a chamber href function, defaulting to current values.
scenario: '#/keep' and '#/chamber/<id>' are baked into the shared kit while ChambersColumn takes hrefs from the caller; an app routing differently gets dead links when on_navigate is absent.
note: Public prop surface change of the shared kit.

title: Seal authority shows raw thrown Error messages to the UI
fix: Map to a fixed reply and log the cause through the existing logger seam.
scenario: seal/tear catch returns cause.message verbatim as the user-visible reply; a transport or local sealer error carrying core internals, paths or request fragments is rendered in the Inspector and notices.
note: Existing authority test pins the verbatim message behaviour.
